calls.head: Ehlers’s line gets the soft minutes
calls.body: At home, the Hurricanes keep sending Ehlers’s line (Ehlers, Stankoven and Blake) out against opponents’ third lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Rod Brind'Amour has been chasing an easier matchup for the team’s scorers. Tonight the Jets’ third line is Iafallo, Lowry and Rosén.

calls.beyond: Carolina has a better power play than most. Even by those standards, this was a big night: 18.1 expected goals per 60 on the power play, against their usual 8.2 (about 8.9 against Winnipeg) and a league average of 7.7. A team strays this far about once every 40 games.

surprises.head: A shutout for Pyotr Kochetkov
surprises.body: Kochetkov stopped all 26 shots, worth 2.9 expected goals. Starting goalies have a night this good about once every 50 starts.

story.head: Nothing gets past Kochetkov
paras: An ugly night for the Jets. Sean Walker, who scores in about 1 game in 11, scored twice. Walker opened the scoring for the Hurricanes shorthanded early in the first. The second period belonged to the Hurricanes. Juuso Välimäki and Sebastian Aho scored 24 seconds apart early in the period to make it 3-0, and the Jets had no answer. Walker and Logan Stankoven scored a minute and a half apart later in the period to stretch the lead to 5-0, and the Jets had no answer. Winnipeg pulled Stuart Skinner after five goals and turned to Clay Stevenson for the rest of the second. Mark Jankowski and Jesperi Kotkaniemi scored less than two minutes apart early in the third to make it 7-0, and the Jets never had an answer. Stankoven finished with a goal and two assists.

The Hurricanes drove the play, outshooting the Jets 32-26, and the scoreboard caught up. Pyotr Kochetkov was perfect for the Canes, 26 saves on 26 shots. Kochetkov has won all ten of his starts this season, already the longest winning run to open a season by any goalie in franchise history. That is also the franchise record for straight wins in one season, one more than Cam Ward (2008-09) and Brandon Bussi (2025-26). No NHL goalie had opened a season with this many straight wins since Jack Campbell won his first eleven in 2020-21. The Hurricanes improved to 12-2-2, still first in the NHL in both points and points percentage. The Jets are seventh in the Central. The Jets are winless in nine (0-7-2).

items.text: Four straight wins for the Hurricanes.
Nikolaj Ehlers has a point in six straight games.
The Hurricanes’ Jaccob Slavin played his 800th NHL game.
The Hurricanes have beaten the Jets five straight times, going back to the 2024-25 season.
